pages.title: Verses Slipped Between Pages
pages.text: A flower that blooms on old bones still knows the color of spring.$(br)A name the tide carried off still remembers the way home.$(br2)Should you meet one of the dead who refuses to bite, lower your sword —$(br)she is no monster; she simply remembers the word 'human' too well.$(br2)Take dawnlight and gold, nine measures in all, and press them into a star.$(br)What that star holds is life — more life than death itself can hold.$(br)Hold it out to her:$(br)where life spills over, the husk of death cannot stand,$(br)and she will remember who she once was.
